analyst_view.overall: Early view: Valencia (19th) go to Vallecas without José Luis Gayà, sent off against Real Madrid, and Jesús Vázquez, his usual stand-in at left-back, is a doubt with a muscle problem. Javier Aguirre's side took 2 of 21 points at Mestalla and ended the Madrid game with 26 fouls and a half-time tunnel scuffle. Rayo, under Beñat San José, are playing amid fan protests against president Presa that already got their home game with Athletic suspended in October.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean slightly higher: San José's Rayo were among the league's top scorers and leakiest defences early in the season, and Valencia's left side is makeshift without Gayà and with Vázquez doubtful. Rayo's last two home games ended 3-0 one way and 0-3 the other, not tight draws.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners. Aguirre's Valencia play a deep 5-3-2 and took only two corners at the Bernabéu, so most of the play should be Rayo crossing into a packed box, which tends to produce blocks and corners. Rayo won six corners even in their defeat at Anoeta.

cards.text: The model has 5.1 cards and I lean higher. Valencia took four yellows and a red against Madrid, Aguirre himself was booked, and there was a tunnel scuffle at half-time. Add a relegation-zone visitor and a tense Vallecas crowd and six or more cards is realistic.

shots.text: The site expects 29.0 shots, 10.7 from Valencia. That looks generous for a Valencia side that managed four shots at Madrid and set up to defend. Rayo should take most of the shots, but one team doing the shooting makes a total in the high 20s a stretch.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target and I am close to that. Rayo should create decent chances against a weakened Valencia back line, but Valencia's own output on target is minimal, so the two effects roughly cancel out.
